record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.original_question: Let γ be a smooth closed strictly convex curve in the plane, and let T be the outer billiard map near γ defined by the rule that the segment joining a point A to its image T(A) is tangent to γ at its midpoint. Besides the ellipse case, for which γ is the outer billiard integrable?

evidence.quote: Question: Are there other integrable outer billiards?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\gamma$ be a smooth closed strictly convex curve in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. For a point $A$ in the unbounded component of $\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus \gamma$ sufficiently close to $\gamma$, there are two tangent lines from $A$ to $\gamma$; choose one of them according to a fixed orientation (say, so that $\gamma$ lies to the right of the directed line from $A$). Let $P$ be the point of tangency of this chosen line with $\gamma$, and define the outer (dual) billiard map $T$ by letting $T(A)$ be the reflection of $A$ through $P$, so that $P$ is the midpoint of the segment joining $A$ to $T(A)$.

The map $T$ is called integrable on a neighborhood $U$ of $\gamma$ in the exterior of $\gamma$ if $U$ is foliated by a continuous one-parameter family of $T$-invariant closed curves, each of which surrounds $\gamma$.

If $\gamma$ is an ellipse, then the outer billiard map $T$ is integrable, with the family of ellipses homothetic to $\gamma$ providing the invariant foliation.

Question: Determine whether there exists a smooth closed strictly convex curve $\gamma$, not an ellipse, such that the outer billiard map $T$ is integrable on some one-sided neighborhood of $\gamma$ in its exterior.
artifact.status_search_result: The general question of whether non-ellipse smooth strictly convex curves can have integrable outer billiards remains open. Partial results exist: Tabachnikov showed that algebraic integrability in a nondegenerate sense forces $\gamma$ to be an ellipse, and a 2024 result of Bialy–Mironov-style rigidity strengthens this under stronger foliation assumptions. The full smooth (non-algebraic) version is still listed as open in recent surveys on billiards.

status_evidence.title: On algebraically integrable outer billiards
status_evidence.snippet: if the outer billiard map around a plane oval is algebraically integrable in a certain nondegenerate sense then the oval is an ellipse

status_evidence.title: Integrable outer billiards and rigidity
status_evidence.snippet: If the exterior of a smooth convex plane curve of positive curvature is foliated by continuous invariant curves of the outer billiard, then the curve must be an ellipse.
status_evidence.claim: A global/total-integrability rigidity version is proved.

status_evidence.title: Integrable Billiards and Related Topics
status_evidence.snippet: the conjecture that ellipses are characterized by their integrability remains an open problem
status_evidence.claim: The local-integrability version of the question is still open.
